text:
Ana: heads-up — after last runtime deploy we saw prefix/prompt cache hit rate drop from ~15% to ~6% across canary GPUs
Tyler: omg. is this kernel selection change (runcode #452) landing in the same release?
Mira: yes, kernel-selector now prefers fused-attn for seq_len<=256. we saw better perf on gen-only tests but not on real traffic.
Sam: quick numbers from profiler on canary (p50 token latency):
```
before: kernel=v1 fused=false  p50=18ms  hit=15%
after:  kernel=v2 fused=true   p50=14ms  hit=6%
KV-cache lookups/sec dropped 2.3x
```
Tyler: interesting — lower token latency but huge hit-rate regression. might be batching/warmup interaction. did the runtime change the warmup/heartbeat probing?
Mira: yes, we added a more aggressive idle-evict to free KV slots when memory pressure high, and we also adjusted the heartbeat probing interval from 60s -> 10s for faster scale-down.
Ana: hypothesis: faster eviction + different kernel startup means clients that rely on prefix warmstart miss more often during short lived bursts -> thundering warmstarts.
Sam: also saw client-side behavior: SDK will retry streaming responses on transient connection errors and the retry path currently toggles X-RW-Cache-Opt: none when streaming_resume=true. that causes cache-opt-out on retries.
SDK Bot: flagged 3 SDK versions that set header X-RW-Cache-Opt=off for streaming retries: 2.4.1, 2.4.2, 2.5.0
Tyler: that seems critical — retries should preserve cache keying. if the SDK unsets opt-in, client retries will miss even if server had warm KV.
Mira: agreed. patch idea: (1) canonicalize client cache key to ignore ephemeral resume tokens, (2) ensure SDK preserves cache-opt header across retries, (3) change heartbeat back to 30s while we validate.
Ana: can we quantify expected hit-rate uplift? run a sim with typical PLG traffic distribution?
Sam: ran a small sim overnight. quick numbers:
```
scenario A (current): heartbeat=10s, sdk-retry-optout -> hit_rate=6%
scenario B (keep heartbeat=30s, sdk-preserve-optin) -> hit_rate=13%
scenario C (B + key-canonicalization) -> hit_rate=16%
```
Mira: good — suggests most of regression is client opt-out + heartbeat. kernel selection still helps p50 latency but we need to tune memory/warmstart policy to avoid killing prefixes too eagerly.
Tyler: action items:
- Mira: roll heartbeat to 30s on canary, add eviction metric per-GPU (ETA today)
- SDK team (Sam): publish patch to preserve X-RW-Cache-Opt across retries, release patch to canary SDK (ETA tomorrow)
- Ana: run A/B sim against product traffic for 24h after canary changes, collect hit_rate, p50, cost-per-token (ETA 48h)
Sam: will also add telemetry: emit header values and whether response was a KV cache hit in traces so we can link client headers -> hit/miss
deploy-bot: started deployment job id=deploy-2026-03-18-752 on cluster canary-3
Ana: thanks. if we get hit back to ~15% we can proceed to full deploy. keep notes here and ping if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
Mira: adding an ephemeral note — when we canonicalize keys, watch out for streaming chunk boundaries; treat "stream-resume-token" as non-keying.
Tyler: also add a small unit test in runtime that asserts cache key invariance across request ordering and resume headers.
Ana: agreed. I'll coordinate follow-ups in a quick doc.
